info.title: Financial Datasets API — Macro Interest Rates
info.description: Central bank interest rate data (historical series + real-time snapshot), proxied through AIsa.

bank.description: The symbol of the central bank.

name.description: The name of the central bank.

rate.description: The interest rate of the central bank.

date.description: The date of the interest rate in YYYY-MM-DD format.

CostEstimate.description: Read-only cost quote for the exact request. No Provider call, billing reservation, durable job, or price lock is created.

currency.description: Quote currency. Always USD in this version.

estimate_kind.description: `exact` is a fully determined customer price; `upper_bound` has a locally enforceable ceiling in `max_cost_micros_usd`; `estimate` depends on terminal usage and may exceed the quoted amount.

estimated_cost_micros_usd.description: Quoted customer cost in micro-USD (1 USD = 1,000,000 micros).

max_cost_micros_usd.description: Optional hard customer-cost ceiling in micro-USD. Present for `exact` and `upper_bound`; omitted for `estimate`.

pricing_version.description: Optional immutable or compiled pricing version.

estimated_at.description: UTC timestamp when the quote was produced.

metadata.description: Bounded non-sensitive quote metadata, such as a canonical model or profile key.

NotFoundError.description: The specified resource was not found

PaymentRequiredError.description: The request requires a paid subscription

example.message: This endpoint requires a paid subscription. Please upgrade your plan.

CostEstimate.description: Read-only cost quote. The intended request is validated but not executed, billed, reserved, or locked.

Cache-Control.description: Quotes are never stored by shared caches.

Vary.description: Response body depends on the cost-mode header.

XAISACostMode.name: X-AISA-Cost-Mode
XAISACostMode.description: Set to `quote` to estimate this exact request without executing data, creating a job, or authorizing spend. A successful quote is HTTP 200 with a `cost_estimate` body; it is not a reservation or price lock. Omit the header for normal execution. Any other value returns `400 invalid_cost_mode`. Quote mode requires an API key and cannot use MPP or x402.

get.description: One central bank's policy rate over time, as an `interest_rates` array of `bank`, `name`, `date` and `rate`. `bank` is required and bound by `start_date` and `end_date`. Trap worth knowing: the code is case-sensitive and must be uppercase — FED works, fed returns HTTP 404 with "No data found", which reads like an empty result rather than a bad argument. Valid codes are FED, ECB, BOJ, BOE, BOC, RBA, PBOC, SNB, RBI and BOK; `get_financial_macro_interest_rates_snapshot` with no arguments lists them all.

parameters.name: bank
parameters.description: The bank whose interest rates to return. Use the /macro/interest-rates/banks endpoint to get a list of available banks. Case-sensitive: must be uppercase. A lowercase code returns HTTP 404 "No data found", which reads like an empty result rather than a bad argument.

parameters.name: start_date
parameters.description: The start date of the interest rates to return in YYYY-MM-DD format.

parameters.name: end_date
parameters.description: The end date of the interest rates to return in YYYY-MM-DD format.

200.description: Interest rates response. When `X-AISA-Cost-Mode` is `quote`, HTTP 200 returns a `cost_estimate` instead of executing this operation. The quote is not a reservation, authorization, or price lock.

get.description: Current policy rates for the ten central banks tracked here, as an `interest_rates` array of `bank`, `name`, `rate` and `date`. `bank` is optional — omit it to get all ten at once, which is also how you discover the valid codes: FED, ECB, BOJ, BOE, BOC, RBA, PBOC, SNB, RBI and BOK. Use it for the current rate backdrop. For one bank's rate path over time use `get_financial_macro_interest_rates`.

parameters.name: bank
parameters.description: Optional central bank code (e.g., FED, ECB, BOJ). AIsa also accepts this endpoint without `bank` and returns the latest snapshot for all major central banks. Case-sensitive: must be uppercase. A lowercase code returns HTTP 404 "No data found", which reads like an empty result rather than a bad argument.

200.description: Interest rates snapshot response. When `X-AISA-Cost-Mode` is `quote`, HTTP 200 returns a `cost_estimate` instead of executing this operation. The quote is not a reservation, authorization, or price lock.
